title: Appearance is below the fold again, because the panel still wants more room than the window has
goal: With a piece of text picked in a three layer document, the right hand panel asks for more height than the tallest window this display can give it, and the section that lost the argument is Appearance: its last stretch now sits below the bottom of the panel where it used to be on screen. You asked on 2026-09-07 that Appearance and Effects are the two sections nobody should ever have to scroll to, and shipped work has quietly walked that back. Decide how the panel keeps that promise when what it wants does not fit, and make it keep it.
notes:
From the 2026-09-16 design review, and the evidence is two rough lines the panel-sections task wrote about its own work (queue/audits/2026-09-15-panel-sections.json):

  "The panel is still over-subscribed by a factor, not by a few points. With a piece of text picked in a three layer document it wants 1052 points and the tallest window this display gives it is 968. Nothing was made shorter; the change only decides which sections are allowed to ask."
  "Appearance pays for it. At 1200 by 720 with text picked it now runs 497 to 720 in a 688 point panel, so its last 32 points are below the fold where they used to be on screen. With an arrow picked it is 382 points tall and lands at 681 in a 688 point panel."
  "This partly walks back what the user asked for on 2026-09-07, that Appearance and Effects are the two sections that must never need scrolling to. It is a real trade and the evaluate list above asks about it directly rather than hiding it."

Why this is filed as its own task rather than folded: the panel's height has now been attacked seven separate times with local fixes, every one of them done (the-panel-stops-explaining-itself-in-paragraphs, picking-a-text-layer-leaves-its-settings-below-t, position-and-size-leave-the-panel, one-row-for-a-number-that-has-four-sides, the-panel-shows-the-panes-that-matter, position-and-size-stays-on-screen-when-you-pick, the-h-field-in-the-text-section-can-be-out-of-re), and the panel still asks for 1052 in a 968. Each of those bought back points. None of them changed the fact that the sections together want more than any window has, which is why the next feature that wants room takes it from Appearance again.

Related and NOT the same thing: photograph-the-sections-row-and-measure-what-it (nobody has seen the Sections row drawn or measured what turning a section off really buys) and the-motion-section-sits-directly-under-effects-w (Motion is eleven sections below Effects). Do those two first if all three are open: this one needs their numbers.
acceptance: With a piece of text picked, Appearance is fully on screen without scrolling, at the window sizes a person actually uses
The same is true of Effects
The rule is written down where the next section to be added will be read against it, so this does not get walked back again by the next feature that wants room
The panel's asked-for height and the height it is given are both measured and reported, before and after, at a window size named in the audit
It is checked with an arrow picked as well as with text, because those two ask for different sections

MEASURED, before any change. The Mac's screen was locked for this whole turn, so no walk could run (every one exits 3 with status locked) and no picture was possible. Instead I read back the 3,334 recorded panel states that 185 walks left in /tmp/photonz-playtest earlier today. At a 1200x720 window the dock is 621pt, 609 shareable; Appearance or Effects was below the fold in 44% of states there, 50% at 781pt, and 12% even at the 969pt dock of the largest window this display opens. Worked cases at 1200x720: text 163+198+231+68=747 (over 126); arrow 163+447+68=765 (over 144); component copy 163+311+195+68=1102 (over 481); measurement 163+109+489+68=702 (over 81).

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, before building: the mock-equivalent here is the seven previous fixes, and they are wrong. All seven were ORDERING changes, and ordering only decides WHICH section is left below the fold, never how many points there are. The thing none of them knew is in the numbers above: Appearance is not a small form, it is the BIGGEST section in the dock. It is a list of the parts a thing is made of and every switched-on part unfolds all of its settings at once (PartsInspector -> ShapePartSettings), so an arrow is 447pt of it and a measurement 489pt. The tallest Appearance recorded all day is 669pt, which is MORE THAN THE WHOLE 621pt DOCK. DockMetrics.scrollingSections still classifies Appearance as a form, so it is the only one of the promised sections the height budget may never shorten. An eighth ordering fix would have walked something else back; I did not write one.

SHIPPED, mechanism-independent: acceptance item 3 (the rule written down where the next section is read against it). Sources/Photonz/InspectorDockLayout.swift now carries a third rule beside the two it already had about order and cast: a rule about HEIGHT, with the budget arithmetic, the four worked cases, the percentages and the two findings. It says a section may not be added, and an existing one may not grow, without naming which line of that table it spends from. That file is what every panel change reads first. swift build clean; Scripts/test.sh green, 7662 tests in 615 suites.

BLOCKED on a decision rather than guessing an eighth time. The three ways out are visibly different products and the arithmetic says no single one covers every case: (a) let the budget shorten Appearance, so the fold is guaranteed by construction and Appearance scrolls inside itself when it must - the only answer that cannot fail; (b) Appearance folds one part at a time like the Effects list, which fixes arrow and measurement but leaves text over by 15pt and a component copy by 93pt; (c) the layers list moves to a left dock, which hands back 163pt and fixes three of four but not a measurement. Recommended (a). Card and brief filed. Acceptance items 1, 2, 4-after and 5 are unverifiable this turn anyway: they all need a walk, and a walk needs an unlocked screen.

left rough, not filed: Appearance is declared a form in DockMetrics.scrollingSections while being a variable-length list of parts. That misclassification is the mechanical cause of everything above, but fixing it IS option (a), so it belongs to this task's decision and not to a task of its own. The shared patterns document has no rule for what a panel column owes when its sections want more height than the window can give: which sections it may push below the fold, what it owes the one it pushes, and what a new section has to prove before it may join the column. Section 3's height rule stops at 'when it still does not fit, the dock scrolls and nothing is thrown away', which says what must not happen and not who loses. The answer to the card on this task settles it, so the rule is written by whoever does this task, not before. ADVERSARIAL REVIEW of the answer before building it. The decision says Appearance scrolls inside itself, and on its own that is NOT enough: I worked it through and with text picked the pair's own floors come to 404 points of a 222 point share (Appearance 112 + Effects 292, where 292 is the room that draws the open drop shadow whole). So a second thing was needed: the budget has to be allowed to squeeze the PROMISED pair under their own floors when that is what the fold costs, and to push what sits below them off the bottom instead. Also rejected: reporting Appearance's parts as PANES so its floor keeps one whole part. It buys nothing in any measured case (the water line hands it 164 where the pane floor would have asked 126) and in the measurement case it made the dock WORSE, trading Motion and Measurements away entirely to give Appearance 82 more points. Shortest version that delivers the value wins.

SHIPPED. Two mechanisms, both needed. (1) DockMetrics.scrollingSections now includes Appearance, so the budget may shorten it: it is a LIST of the parts a thing is made of, not a form, and calling it a form is why it was the one promised section the budget could never touch. That alone fits a rectangle, an arrow and a measurement. (2) DockHeightBudget gains promisedSections and foldRescue: when the ordinary pass leaves one of the promised pair hanging past the bottom edge, it re-shares the dock down to the LAST promised section, letting the pair go under their own floors as far as foldFloor (74), and lets everything below them go below the fold. That is what fits a piece of text with its shadow open, where the pair's own floors came to 404 points of a 222 point share. A promised section holding room for a pane you JUST OPENED drops out of the promise, so the opened effect is still drawn whole - the mitigation the decision card offered. Measured after, off dock-picked-first-walk at viewport 661: text drawn Layers 6-170, Text 170-368, Appearance 368-514, Effects 514-660 (was 650-975); arrow drawn Layers 6-224, Appearance 224-424, Effects 424-492, Motion 492-573, Measurements 573-660, so the whole panel fits for the first time. dockInView lists Appearance and Effects in every one of the twelve dock states that walk records.

Two things fixed on the way, both found by walks going red rather than by reading. (a) A walk reaching a control inside a shortened section picked its scroller BY GEOMETRY - every scroller whose scrolled length covered that patch of window - because a press target is a point and a box rather than a view. With two shortened sections in the panel that is wrong: Appearance's unseen tail covers the stretch of window the Effects list had scrolled a Border into, so the reveal turned Appearance's wheel and reported the Border 'covered by something other than a scroll'. PlaytestPressTarget now carries the clips that really hold it, off the view tree (PlaytestPanelPress.scrollClips). Broke appearance-list-walk, effects-open-into-view-walk and effects-room-for-the-one-you-opened-walk; all green after. (b) scrollEdgeFade was a BRANCH around the scroller, so a list crossing the shortened threshold got a brand new scroller - losing where it was scrolled to, and in separate-whole-screenshot-walk losing the rows themselves (the panel held no rows at all after two undos took the list from shortened to whole). It is a flag inside the modifier now.

FILED: the-panel-keeps-its-promise-on-a-video-document (the one case the guarantee does NOT cover: the timing strip takes 235 points off the dock, which leaves 99 for the pair however it is shared, so on a laptop video document the panel drops the guarantee and scrolls as before - reproduction is a test that passes, DockFoldGuaranteeTests.aDockTooShortForThePairIsLeftToScrollRatherThanStarved) and the-section-you-are-using-is-the-one-you-scroll (the four ORDER complaints this task collected but did not fix: Sound's Level fader lowest in the dock, Speed six sections down, Time under Reframe and Motion, a title's Fade below the fold - rule 5 now says everything below the pair MAY be pushed, so which sections deserve to be up there is its own question). LEFT ROUGH, not filed: the fade on a squeezed Appearance is subtle in the text case - the section simply ends under Blending and the 14 point gradient reads more like padding than a cut; it is clearer wherever the cut lands mid-row, and the audit asks the user about it rather than my guessing. Also left rough: PartsInspector's Opacity row scrolls away with the rest of Appearance when it could have been pinned as non-scrolling chrome the way the layers list pins its count line; it needs the section split into a fixed head and a scrolling body, which CollapsibleSection does not offer, and nothing measured says it is worth that.

The fold is guaranteed: Appearance and Effects are both whole in the panel on every layer. Appearance joined the sections the budget may shorten (it is a list of parts, not a form), and DockHeightBudget.foldRescue re-shares the dock down to the last promised section when the ordinary pass leaves one of them hanging, pushing what sits below them below the fold instead; a pane you just opened is exempt, so an opened effect is still drawn whole. Measured at 1200x720 (dock 661): text was Appearance 367-650 / Effects 650-975 and is now 368-514 / 514-660; an arrow was Appearance 169-667 with three sections under it off screen and now the whole panel fits 6-660. Rule written into UX-PATTERNS section 3 (height rule 5, rule 2 corrected, rule 4 widened, section 9 gate) and the HEIGHT section of InspectorDockLayout.swift. Also: a cut layers list now fades its edge, and two harness faults found by red walks are fixed. 11 new core tests in DockFoldGuaranteeTests; 68 walks green including dock-picked-first-walk, which this task owned and which was failing on exactly this; Scripts/test.sh green but for the known export-size flake.
